questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following animals is capable of hibernating for up to three years?
A. Bat B. Bear C. Snail
Answer: C. The record for the longest hibernation is held by desert snails, which can seal themselves in their shells and go dormant for years, surviving even in museum collections.
questions.de: Welche Tiere können sich in ihrem Gehäuse verschließen und jahrelang ruhen – ein Wüstenexemplar, 1846 im British Museum auf eine Karte geklebt, wurde 1850 lebend entdeckt?
questions.en: Which animals can seal themselves in their shells and stay dormant for years — one desert specimen glued to a card at the British Museum in 1846 was found alive in 1850?

timeline.labelEn: A desert snail (Eremina desertorum) glued to a card at the British Museum is found alive four years later
timeline.labelDe: Eine im British Museum auf eine Karte geklebte Wüstenschnecke (Eremina desertorum) wird vier Jahre später lebend entdeckt

questions.notes: The card's 'up to three years' is a popular figure; the documented British Museum specimen (Eremina desertorum) revived after about four years, and in a 1904–1912 experiment some sealed snails survived about eight years. Snail dormancy in heat/drought is aestivation rather than hibernation.

questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] What is the meaning of “poke,” the Hawaiian dish?
A. To cut B. Raw C. Fish
Answer: A. In Hawaiian, “poke” means “to slice” or “to cut into chunks,” which refers to the preparation method of the dish, typically involving raw fish. Historically, poke evolved from the practice of fishermen seasoning the cut-offs from their catch to serve as a snack.
questions.de: Was bedeutet das hawaiische Wort „Poke“, der Name des Gerichts aus rohem Fisch?
questions.en: What does the Hawaiian word “poke”, the name of the raw-fish dish, mean?

timeline.labelEn: Poke in its present form becomes popular in Hawaii
timeline.labelDe: Poke in seiner heutigen Form wird auf Hawaii populär

questions.notes: Wikipedia: 'to slice' or 'cut crosswise into pieces'; 'to cut' accepted.
